describes: The Hohfeldian incidents — the jurisdiction-neutral analytic layer beneath the deontic modals. Eight positions in four correlative pairs, with jural correlatives and jural opposites as checkable relations.

incidents.name: claim
incidents.gloss: a right that another perform (or forbear)

incidents.name: duty
incidents.gloss: an obligation owed to a claim-holder

incidents.name: privilege
incidents.gloss: a liberty to act; no duty either way (Hohfeld's liberty)

incidents.name: no-right
incidents.gloss: the absence of a claim against a privilege-holder

incidents.name: power
incidents.gloss: the ability to change legal positions (waive, consent, terminate, assign)

incidents.name: disability
incidents.gloss: the absence of a power (no capacity to change positions)

correlatives.describes: Jural correlatives: if one party holds the left, the counterparty holds the right, over the same act.

opposites.describes: Jural opposites: the negation of a position for the same party.
